hypothesis: Deep CPU idle states (C2 127 us, C3 1048 us exit latency) on the audio cores add wake-up latency that makes audio blocks late; holding PM QoS /dev/cpu_dma_latency at 10 us (C1 only) lowers Live's DSP load, its peaks and PipeWire errors.

change.switch: /dev/cpu_dma_latency = 10 us held for the run (PM QoS)

rationale: No Set improved beyond the A/A spread on DSP average or typical peak (Inbuilts -0.3/+0.5, Max4Live -0.1/+0.5, VSTs -0.2/+0.5 pt); PipeWire errors 63 (A) vs 73 (B) and peaks over 100% 18 vs 18 across 15 Set-runs per arm. The cap held: 0 C2/C3 entries during B runs vs about 7 million per A run. Deep idle states are not what causes the dropouts.

hypothesis: pipeasio-rt, the thread that starts every audio block, runs SCHED_OTHER under PipeASIO's shipped realtime=false while all of Live's threads run SCHED_RR 10 (launcher chrt -r 10), so it waits about 650 ms per 30 s for a CPU; PIPEASIO_REALTIME=1 removes that wait and with it late blocks and dropouts.

rationale: Mechanism confirmed: pipeasio-rt ran SCHED_FIFO 15 in every B run and its CPU wait fell from 595-706 ms to 1.2-2.4 ms per 30 s. Dropouts fell: PipeWire errors 67 -> 32 and peaks over 100% 13 -> 9 across 15 Set-runs per arm (Max4Live 36 -> 15, VSTs 13 -> 5). Live's DSP meter is mixed within about 2x the A/A spread: Max4Live average -1.5 (1.9x) and typical peak -0.7 (1.75x), VSTs typical peak -1.2 and worst peak -17.5, Inbuilts average +1.3 (1.1x). Not yet beyond 2x on a primary metric: confirm with longer, dropout-focused windows (T0003).

hypothesis: Confirmation of T0002 with dropout-focused 120 s windows on the three heavy Sets: PIPEASIO_REALTIME=1 runs pipeasio-rt, the thread that calls bufferSwitch for every block, at SCHED_FIFO 15 instead of SCHED_OTHER under Live's SCHED_RR 10 threads, which removes its CPU wait and with it most PipeWire errors, without making Live's DSP load worse.
